## S6 CLOSED -- epic 6202's precondition chain is done, S1 dispatched

09da (S6, bounded gate admission) closed after its re-review passed clean. The epic's chain has now
run in the right order: S0 (ADR 0112, merged and closed) -> S6 (bounded concurrency, the precondition)
-> S1 (dedicated gate-scratch volume), which 'rebar ready --epic' now returns as the only ready child.

That ordering was the whole point of the ADR work: the janitor reclaims by high-water mark over POSIX
delete-on-last-close, so bytes held by an in-flight gate are LIVE rather than garbage, and a disk cap
below peak concurrent hold cannot be honoured by reclamation at all. Capping concurrency first is what
makes S2-S5's caps meaningful.

S1 dispatched with two constraints stated up front rather than discovered:
 - TERRAFORM MAY BE WRITTEN AND VALIDATED, NEVER APPLIED. terraform apply is an operator-authorised
   action on live infrastructure; fmt and validate are fine, a plan against real state is out of scope.
 - DECLARE EVERY FILE IN file_impact BEFORE REVIEW, INCLUDING NEW ONES. S6 lost a full re-review cycle
   to this, and the file it forgot to declare was the new module at the centre of its own change. That
   is worth passing on as a rule rather than letting the next agent rediscover it.
Also told it to check REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR first, since that already parameterises the snapshot store's
base dir and a large part of 'move gate scratch to its own volume' may be configuration plus
provisioning rather than new code -- do not build a mechanism where a config path already exists.

And the ADR consequence it must honour: an unreachable scratch volume is a REFUSAL, not a silent
fallback to the root filesystem. S6 already implemented that split
(GateScratchUnavailableError refuses; a missing fcntl admits-and-announces), so there is a working
precedent in-tree.

Running totals: NINE changes merged tonight (2593, 2596, 2600, 2614, 2594, 2607, 2601, 2609, 2613),
SIX tickets closed (3a02, 9a17, c379, 740d, 477b, 09da). Main is still red on sweep (macos, full
suite) -- 2618 is the only thing that clears it, and it is being reworked after failing pytest
ubuntu py3.12.
